title: Roadmap & Launch Readiness - Product + Eng Sync
summary: Product and Engineering reviewed launch readiness for the upcoming 2025-05 milestone. Key open items: finalize perf benchmarks, complete runbooks and incident playbooks, schedule final canary, and confirm SLOs and alerting. Discussed root cause and mitigations from the March incident and adjustments to quantization/kv cache handling.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-04-10 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~60m | Attendees: Aisha, Daniel, Sofia, Ethan, Maya, Ravi

Summary: quick sync on roadmap milestones for May launch, readiness checklist, and incident review from March outage to ensure we won't repeat.

[00:00] Aisha: Alright everyone, thanks for jumping on. We have an hour, we'll run through the launch readiness checklist, update on benchmarks, and then do a short incident review from the March outage. Daniel, can you kick us off with perf?

[00:30] Daniel: Yeah, sure. So I ran the 512-token benchmarks on both p3 and a100 last week, numbers look close to the infra team's targets but there's a tail at high conc that spikes. We suspect the batching logic under high concurrency plus a KV cache lock contention. The median latency is fine but p99 is around 720ms on a100 when concurrent requests hit 200+ in the same pool.

[01:15] Ethan: That lines up with observability — we saw autoscaler not spin up quickly enough during the March event, and then the cache fills and causes serialized access. Also memory pressure on the nodes triggered eviction which slowed down the runtime.

[01:45] Maya: From QA side, the regression tests passed for the model change but we didn't simulate cross-tenant bursts which is what caused the March incident to cascade. We should add a multi-tenant burst test to the pre-canary suite.

[02:10] Aisha: Good, so action item: add multi-tenant burst scenarios. Daniel, can you add that to the benchmark runs and include a histogram of concurrency levels?

[02:25] Daniel: Yep. I'll update the benchmark sheet and include concurrency buckets. Link will be in the notes.

[03:00] Sofia: Quick note about UX — we need to be explicit in the console about what "dedicated pool burst" means in the docs so PMs and SREs know expected behavior; users kept confusing burst capacity with infinite headroom.

[03:30] Aisha: Good point. We'll add a doc blurb and a tooltip.

[04:00] Ethan: On the incident review, root cause summary: March 12th outage traced to a combination of aggressive quantization rollout and a KV cache edge-case causing excessive cache thrashing. The quantized model variant used a memory layout that increased cache misses under certain sequence length distributions, and our fallback wasn't robust — the runtime attempted a hot-path kernel we hadn't fully stress tested.

[05:00] Daniel: To be precise, the runtime chose an optimized attention kernel for the quantized path which has a different memory stride; under long prefixes with frequent cache invalidations it serialized some critical sections. That plus slow autoscaler led to queueing and timeouts.

[05:30] Ravi: We fixed the immediate issue by reverting the quantized variant and tweaking the autoscaler thresholds, but we need a long-term fix — either make the kernel selection more conservative for certain seq length distributions, or add a KV cache lock-free path.

[06:05] Aisha: Let's enumerate possible mitigations and decide before the canary: 1) change kernel selection policy to avoid the risky optimized kernel for quantized models by default, 2) improve KV cache locking to reduce contention, 3) run more aggressive autoscaler tests and lower the scale-up thresholds for canary traffic. Thoughts?

[06:40] Daniel: I favor 1 and 3 as lower-risk for launch. Kernel changes require deep testing across models and may introduce perf regressions we don't have time for. Improving cache internals is ideal but higher engineering cost. Autoscaler thresholds we can change quickly and validate.

[07:15] Ethan: Agree. Also we can implement a runtime toggle to force a safe kernel selection for the canary that we flip off after we validate. That buys us time.

[07:40] Maya: For QA, we'll need a test matrix that includes quantized+long-prefix+high-concurrency. I'll add that to the checklist.

[08:05] Aisha: Okay, immediate decisions: keep quantized rollout paused for canary, use a safe kernel forced flag for canary, lower autoscaler thresholds for the canary pools. Daniel and Ravi will work the autoscaler and kernel-flag config. Ethan will update the incident runbook and lead tabletop. Maya will expand tests.

[08:30] Sofia: On the docs front, I'll draft the console tooltip and a short "What to expect" doc for burst behavior; entry-level language for PMs and ops.

[09:00] Aisha: Great. Next, observability and SLOs — we need to finalize the SLOs we'll promise for the release. Proposed: 99th percentile latency target for hosted API at <=500ms for typical workloads and <=800ms for peak bursts; SREs weigh in.

[09:40] Ethan: Those are reasonable as targets, but our historical p99 for some models is already hovering around 600ms under realistic loads. To hit 500ms we'll need batching/caching tweaks or smaller model variants for the default offering. For canary we should set a temporary SLO of 800ms and then tighten post-canary.

[10:15] Aisha: Ok set canary SLO 800ms p99. Action: Aisha to document SLOs in the playbook.

[10:35] Daniel: Regarding rollout plan: proposed timeline — internal canary 2025-04-20 to 2025-04-24, expand to beta customers 2025-04-28 to 2025-05-02, GA 2025-05-09. We should keep a one-week buffer between beta and GA to address any issues.

[11:05] Ravi: Confirming infra: dedicated pool autoscaler config will be set for canary pools with lower scale-up thresholds and a burst buffer of 20% capacity. I'll validate configs by 2025-04-15.

[11:35] Aisha: Good. Communication plan — Marketing to pre-announce, but we need to lock the performance claims. We should not advertise 500ms p99 until we hit it post-GA. Aisha will coordinate with Growth.

[12:00] Sofia: Quick UX ask: add a per-route latency breakdown in the console for the canary to help support diagnose issues live. Small change but very helpful.

[12:25] Ethan: On alerting, add a composite alert that trips when p99 > 900ms for 5m and error rate > 0.5% — that will trigger on-staff and PagerDuty. Also add an early-warning alert if scaling events exceed X per minute.

[13:00] Maya: QA schedule: pre-canary smoke tests on 2025-04-17, full regression + multi-tenant bursts on 2025-04-18, then signed off by 2025-04-19.

[13:30] Aisha: Perfect. Anything else on launch readiness?

[14:00] Daniel: One more thing — we need a runbook step to quickly rollback to the previous non-quantized model variant and to pin model versions per-route. That was messy in March. I'll add a CLI shortcut to pin and revert.

[14:30] Ravi: Also audit logs — make sure the private deployment docs include steps to check KMS rotations and audit trail for the canary customers. Compliance asked for that.

[15:00] Aisha: Good note. Let's go into the incident timeline quick recap for the notes: March 12 14:07 UTC saw onset, autoscaler lagged, queue grew, runtime picked the optimized quantized kernel leading to KV cache contention causing many requests to timeout; mitigation was revert and scale-up. We added short-term fixes and improved monitoring. Full root cause doc will be linked.

[16:00] Ethan: I'll add logs and the timeline to the incident doc and link it.

[16:30] Aisha: Closing—recap of next steps: Daniel benchmark + concurrency histograms, Ravi validate autoscaler for canary, Ethan draft incident runbook and run tabletop, Maya expand QA tests, Sofia doc changes, Aisha finalize playbook and SLOs. We'll reconvene 2025-04-16 for a pre-canary readiness check.

[17:00] Daniel: Sounds good.

[17:10] Sofia: Thanks all.

[17:15] Meeting ends.

Notes/links: Benchmark sheet (link placeholder), Incident root cause doc (link placeholder), Launch playbook draft (link placeholder).

Transcription notes: occasional speaker label noise and mis-hearings (e.g., "kv cash" vs "kv cache", "a100" occasionally transcribed as "a one-zero-zero"), some overlapping crosstalk during quick Q&A.
